title: Identity compatibility for section-normalized ordinary reindexing
statement: Fix a prime l and a finite field extension E of Q_l in universe u. Let A be a PodReindexFamily l E [def-pod-completion-reindex-coherence]. Suppose its completion and tensor components satisfy PodCompletionReindex.Laws [def-pod-completion-reindex-models] and PodCompletedTensorReindex.Laws [def-pod-completion-tensor-normalization] for every isomorphism between schemes on which l is invertible. If its identity comparison is the specified Over.mapId restriction on every original local section, then A.Identity l E holds: its reduction, total-limit and completed-tensor comparisons satisfy the three identity equations of [def-pod-completion-reindex-coherence]. Only this one comparison is required to be section-normalized; no other coherence law is assumed.

source.place: Steps 1 and 5: identity and composition of the normalized quotient, Roos-limit and tensor transport.

proof.text: Apply podIdentityLimit, which proves the limit identity from the section normalization and the completion Laws by the strict restricted-tower calculation, both Roos coordinates, normalized K-injective models and localization.

Use the unit compatibility of the completion datum and the limit identity. Under the adjunction homEquiv, the inverse reduction comparison followed by the system identity agrees with reduction of the ordinary identity, by unit naturality. Injectivity of homEquiv and cancellation of the reduction isomorphism give the reduction equation. No counit hypothesis is needed.

On good representatives, podIdentityTensorRoos identifies the whole tensor cochain comparison followed by the two degreewise identity maps. Apply the representative Model equality. Naturality of integralCompletedTensorComparison and the derived identity factor formula allow cancellation of that model isomorphism, proving the tensor identity on representatives. Essential surjectivity of the good localization supplies representatives for both constructible inputs; constructibility is invariant under their isomorphisms. Naturality of the tensor comparison and ordinary derived identity transports the equation to the original inputs.

lean.statement:
theorem podReindexingIdentityCompatibility
    (A : PodReindexFamily l E)
    (hcompletion : ∀ {V W : Scheme.{u}} (f : V ⟶ W) [IsIso f]
      [∀ v : V, Invertible (l : V.residueField v)]
      [∀ w : W, Invertible (l : W.residueField w)],
      PodCompletionReindex.Laws l E f (A.completion f))
    (htensor : ∀ {V W : Scheme.{u}} (f : V ⟶ W) [IsIso f]
      [∀ v : V, Invertible (l : V.residueField v)]
      [∀ w : W, Invertible (l : W.residueField w)],
      PodCompletedTensorReindex.Laws l E f (A.completion f) (A.tensor f))
    (hidentity : ∀ (W : Scheme.{u}) (M : scalarReductionSource l E W) (U : W.ProEt)
      (x : M.val.obj (op ((proEtaleIsoPostcompose (𝟙 W)).obj U))),
      ((A.identity W).hom.app M).val.app (op U) x =
        M.val.map ((MorphismProperty.Over.mapId (P := @WeaklyEtale) ⊤ W
          (𝟙 W) rfl).hom.app U).op x) :
    A.Identity l E
